name: Brand + legal clearance
description: USPTO/EUIPO classes 9 and 42 for 'Ibex Cairn'; coexistence opinion vs IBEX Limited (NASDAQ:IBEX), Ibexa AS and Reg 5985152; acquire ibexcairn.com; GitHub org + npm scope; Azure Marketplace name check
notes: Screening done (docs/legal/S00-trademark-screening.md): domains/org/npm all free BUT live US Reg 5985152 'IBEX' covers Classes 9+42 for software integrating and automating separate software systems - our exact category. Needs an attorney opinion before any brand spend. Renaming is still nearly free

name: Upstream licence review
description: Read LICENSE and usage terms of Azure/logicapps-migration-agent; formal opinion on commercial redistribution of a fork; decide fork vs hybrid fallback
notes: RESOLVED: verbatim MIT, no rider or field-of-use restriction. Commercial fork permitted, ADR-0001 Accepted, S02 released. verified=no until counsel glance + transitive dependency licence scan land. See docs/legal/S01-upstream-licence-review.md

name: Headless core extraction
description: Fork upstream; lift src/parsers/** and src/ir/** into a standalone TS library with zero vscode imports; strip Microsoft telemetry deps; sever the proprietary ms-azuretools.vscode-azurelogicapps extensionDependency; ship THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES; prove a CLI emits valid ir.json from a real BizTalk project
notes: SPIKE DONE (docs/specs/002-headless-extraction.md): extraction is mechanical. 16 of 18 vscode-coupled parser files use only CancellationToken; ParserPluginLoader deletes; ir/ has 1 coupled file; telemetry isolated to 1 file. 26451 of 63460 lines lift. Upstream does not clone on Windows without core.longpaths. Extraction itself needs the S03 scaffold

name: Repo scaffold + CI
description: TS monorepo layout, build, lint, unit test harness, GitHub Actions with Windows build agents; fixture corpus of sample BizTalk artefacts; no vscode dependency in core packages
notes: Spec 001 step 1 built. pnpm workspace, 4 packages (core-types/rates/cost/cli), tsc project refs, vitest, eslint type-checked, prettier. install+build+test+lint+help all green locally on Windows; vscode guard proven to fail on a planted import. verified=no until CI confirms the ubuntu matrix leg. BizTalk fixture corpus deferred to S02/S05 (no parser yet to consume it)

name: LLM provider abstraction
description: ILlmProvider interface; Claude API implementation server-side; VS Code LM API as optional local provider; port the 13 upstream skill Markdown files as prompt assets
notes: Built packages/llm: ILlmProvider, ClaudeProvider (Anthropic Messages API, injectable fetch), FakeLlmProvider, SkillLoader with folded-scalar frontmatter parser. 13 BizTalk skills ported from upstream (MIT, NOTICE included). 22 tests green (llm: 10); no network in tests. VS Code LM provider intentionally lives in the editor client, not packages/ (headless guard). verified=no until ubuntu CI leg observed

name: Ingest engine
description: Engine 0: accept GitHub repo / folder / zip / MSI; MSI decomposition; platform auto-detection; normalised workspace; artefact inventory with parse-error reporting
notes: Case workspaces hold customer source - must never be committed

name: IR extension
description: Add targetPlan layer (chosen composition, rejected alternatives + eliminating constraint, cost curve, confidence) and volumetrics annotations; schema validation; versioning strategy
notes: See ADR-0002. Do not let targetPlan become Logic-Apps-shaped

name: Dependency graph + flow grouping
description: Engine 1a: build the artefact dependency graph; detect logical flow groups; resolve cross-application references
notes: This graph is also the as-is diagram source - see S16

name: Complexity + gap scoring
description: Engine 1b: per-flow complexity score; severity-ranked gap list; flag convoys, correlation sets, compensation and custom assemblies for human review
notes: Gaps are a product surface, not an internal log. See docs/06-hard-problems.md

name: Volumetrics harvester
description: Read BizTalkDTADb tracking and BizTalkMsgBoxDb subscriptions: messages/month per flow, avg + p95 size, hourly peakiness, duration, retry/suspend rates. Manual-entry model with measured|assumed tagging
notes: Reads a BizTalk database directly, so not blocked by ingest or by S01. Code cannot reveal traffic. Manual path must be genuinely good, not a downgrade

name: Disposition engine
description: Label every artefact retire | reuse | lift | encapsulate | remain | stay | migrate | rewrite | blocked with 12-month traffic evidence attached; detect duplicate maps and dead ports; consume the portability tier from S38
notes: Cheapest migration is the one you don't do. Runs before placement. Vocabulary spans the portability ladder - ADR-0008

name: Archetype classifier
description: Declarative YAML policy classifying flows into the 11 archetypes; LLM fallback for ambiguous flows only; emit candidate compositions (trigger + compute + state + exposure)
notes: Policy is versioned and customer-tunable; overrides feed back as training signal

name: Rate card client
description: Azure Retail Prices API client (per region, per SKU); caching; offline fixture snapshots; regression suite with one fixture per billing rule
notes: Spec 001 step 2 built. Meter catalogue with drift tripwires, HttpRetailClient with pagination, LiveRateCard (TTL cache) + FixtureRateCard, reproducible capture script. Real eastus fixture captured from the live API (11 meters; connector prices exact, WS1 derived $182.32). 12 tests green incl. offline drift detection; no test touches the network. Drift detection proven live (caught a 2-row Functions meter). verified=no until ubuntu CI leg observed. Per-billing-rule fixtures land in S13

name: Cost model + crossover engine
description: cost(placement, volume, rate_card) as a pure function; executions, actions per execution, connector-call class, storage transactions, duration, egress; cost curves across volume decades; crossover threshold detection
notes: Spec 001 step 3. Takes volumetrics and placement as arguments, so needs neither S09 nor S11 to build or test. LLM never produces a number - see ADR-0004. Standard includes built-in connectors; Consumption meters every action

name: Constraint filter
description: Hard filters applied after classification: message size >256KB, ordering/sessions, VNet, latency SLO, transactionality, EDI, adapter availability, custom .NET, data residency; framework-target coupling (Logic Apps local functions 4.7.2 vs Functions isolated worker 4.8)
notes: Constraints override price. Retarget decision is coupled to the placement decision - ADR-0008

name: Portfolio optimiser
description: Bin-pack flows onto shared hosts subject to blast radius, deploy cadence, scaling profile, security boundary, SLA tier; emit the shared landing zone once; savings waterfall attribution; hybrid-estate TCO including retained BizTalk licence, VMs and support for tier 4-5 flows
notes: Usually saves more than all per-flow decisions combined. Hybrid TCO is a named output, not a caveat - ADR-0008

name: Architecture Design engine
description: Engine 3: as-is, proposed and landing-zone diagrams rendered from the graph via C4/Structurizr to Mermaid, plus draw.io XML with Azure icons; per-flow sequence diagrams from the action DAG; ADR generation
notes: Topology derived from graph, never generated. LLM writes labels and narrative only

name: Assessment report + traceability
description: Engine 8 v1: assessment pack (inventory, disposition, placement with priced curves, diagrams, portfolio TCO vs BizTalk baseline); traceability matrix; runs continuously off the artefact store
notes: P1 EXIT GATE: an independent architect must agree with the conclusions for 3 real apps

name: Emitter framework
description: Task/Step architecture with SPI-style registration (pattern from mule-migration-assistant); machine-readable gap report; template-first, LLM only for the tail
notes: Any design assuming a single emitter is wrong - ADR-0002

name: Logic Apps Standard emitter
description: workflow.json and connections.json, stateful and stateless variants; .NET Framework 4.7.2 local functions for lifted assemblies incl. calls from XSLT maps; project scaffolding; stateless-by-default where the IR proves no waits and no run-history need
notes: SCOPE PENDING ADR-0006: may become 'wrap upstream converter' instead of building our own. Mine BizTalkMigrationStarter ODXtoWFMigrator and the upstream dotnet-local-functions skill

name: Functions + Durable emitter
description: C# Function project, Flex Consumption config, bindings; isolated worker on .NET Framework 4.8 for lifted legacy assemblies; Durable orchestrations and entities for convoy/aggregator archetypes
notes: The cheap target for high-volume and enterprise-connector flows. Isolated worker gives process isolation for 2010-era dependency closures

name: Legacy encapsulation emitter
description: Portability tier 3 and 4 targets: Windows container on Container Apps or AKS Windows node pool for COM/32-bit/P-Invoke components; on-prem exposure via Logic Apps Hybrid, on-premises data gateway or self-hosted API for tier 4
notes: Tiers 3-4 of the portability ladder need their own templates, cost profiles and parity expectations - ADR-0008

name: Messaging + APIM emitter
description: Service Bus topology (queues, topics, subscription rules, sessions, claim-check to Blob); Event Grid; API Management OpenAPI plus policy XML
notes: Routing as configuration - often zero compute

name: Transformation emitter
description: Lift plain XSLT verbatim; .btm to Data Mapper .lml; Liquid where appropriate; extract scripting functoids to functions; database functoids to explicit lookup steps
notes: Verbatim XSLT lift is the cheapest win in the whole migration

name: Golden-pair harvester
description: Extract real input/output message pairs from BizTalk tracking history and Mule logs; these are the specification and already exist; storage and indexing per flow AND per component, so source-less assemblies can be characterised before tiering
notes: No customer writes test cases. Component-level pairs make 'we lost the source in 2014' survivable - ADR-0008

name: Parity harness
description: Engine 6: local replay via Functions Core Tools + Azurite + Docker; canonicalise (namespace prefixes, attribute and key order, whitespace, timestamps, generated GUIDs) then diff; per-flow parity score; promotion gate
notes: P1b EXIT GATE: a published per-flow parity number. This is the moat

name: Development engine
description: Engine 5: environment-in-the-loop agent; branch and PR per flow; build and test in sandbox; failing case + expected + actual fed back as next iteration input; single-flow retry/refine
notes: Cannot promote its own output - the parity harness decides

name: MuleSoft parser
description: Replace the upstream stub: flows, subflows, connector configs, error-handler hierarchies, property placeholders and environment configs, pom.xml, MUnit tests, DataWeave extraction
notes: Second source platform proves the IR is neutral, not BizTalk-shaped

name: DataWeave translation
description: Treat as language translation with generated tests: harvest payload pairs, generate a test per pair, translate, iterate to green; fall back to an emitted C# function and record it in the gap list
notes: No prior art exists anywhere. Budget as research, not a feature

name: Case store + versioning
description: Typed artefact store; every engine writes versioned artefacts with confidence score and gap list; replay from any stage; case fork (clone at 10x volume)
notes: ADR-0003. Engines never communicate through chat

name: Orchestrator + gates + audit
description: Engine 9 on Durable Functions; case state machine; hard human gates at Placement, Plan and Deployment; audit timeline capturing approver, timestamp and override reason
notes: Override reasons feed back into the placement policy

name: Web UI shell
description: Portfolio dashboard across all applications; the 8-node stage rail with badges, expanded active node showing sub-task in words, and six states where awaiting-input/approval are visually distinct from failed; SSE live state; resumability
notes: UI is a pure projection of the artefact store - no separate UI state

name: Web UI assessment screens
description: Load project (GitHub app, upload, on-prem agent, tracking-DB connect); Analysis (inventory tree, dependency graph, editable disposition with traffic sparkline); Cost validation (volumetrics with measured|assumed tags, placement overrides, savings waterfall); Design document viewer with as-is/proposed toggle and export
notes: Cost validation is the screen that sells the product

name: Web UI delivery screens
description: Development board per flow with agent activity stream; Verification parity dashboard with canonicalised message diff viewer; Deployment environment matrix, wave planner, IaC diff, shadow-run comparison, rollback

name: Multi-tenancy + RBAC
description: Tenant isolation, authentication, roles (architect, developer, approver, viewer), secret handling, VPC/on-prem deployment option for regulated customers
notes: Approval gates are meaningless without RBAC

name: Deployment engine
description: Engine 7: Bicep or Terraform emission, CI/CD pipelines, wave rollout, shadow/parallel-run comparison, cutover checklist, rollback

name: FinOps recalibration loop
description: Ingest Azure Cost Management actuals and Application Insights telemetry post-wave; diff against estimate; recalibrate cost model coefficients; actual-vs-estimate reporting
notes: Turns a one-shot tool into recurring revenue. The one asset a later competitor cannot copy

name: MuleSoft target emitter
description: Second non-Azure target, unlocking BizTalk to MuleSoft; proves the hub-and-spoke claim rather than asserting it
notes: Open question: genuine market or positioning claim? See docs/08-roadmap.md

name: Additional source parsers
description: TIBCO BusinessWorks, Dell Boomi, IBM IIB/ACE; upstream already publishes IR examples for all three as templates
notes: P4 EXIT GATE: two targets and four sources through one unchanged IR

name: Portability scanner
description: Scan every assembly for target framework, 32/64-bit, COM references, P/Invoke declarations, references to BizTalk runtime assemblies (IBaseMessage, ExplorerOM, context properties), MSMQ and MSDTC usage, GAC and strong-name dependencies, licensed third-party libraries; assign a portability tier 0-6 deterministically
notes: Reads .NET assemblies from a path, so not blocked by ingest or by S01. Deterministic analysis, not judgement. Feeds S10 disposition and S14 constraints - ADR-0008
